S. 202 ENGR. APRONADO M. IDO Punong Barangay Barangay Abijilan, Municipality of Garcia-Hernandez, Province of Bohol Dear Engr. Ido: This has reference to the letter you sent dated 29 September 2019, requesting for this Department's clarification as to whom special patent is issued in relation to the application for title of your barangay with the Department of Environment and Natural Resources. In your letter, a brief background of the facts states that your barangay applied for a special patent for your barangay lot with the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Tagbilaran City. However, you were informed by the Land Management Bureau (LMB) that under Section 6 of DENR Administrative Order No. 2016-21 (DAO 2016-21)5, the barangays are not expressly mentioned as one of the local government units (LGUs) to whom a special patent shall be issued. Moreover, the LMB cited that under the Local Government Code (LGC), the barangays have no separate corporate personality from their respective cities and/or municipalities, thus, granting land under the name of your barangay may not be feasible and/or legally questionable. Instead, the lot will be named under the municipality. Under this premise arose the request for clarification and legal opinion regarding two issues: (I) Whether the barangay have no separate corporate personality under the LGC and; (2) Whether granting special patent under the name of barangay is not allowed and legally questionable. At the outset, this Department deems it imperative to cite no less than the 1987 Philippine Constitution itself, which states that: 5 DENR Administrative Order No. 2016-21 entitled "Guidelines Governing the Processing of Requests for Proclamations and Issuance of Special Patents Over Agricultural Lands" dated 30 June 2016.

ARTICLE X Local Government General Provisions SECTION I. The territorial and political subdivisions of the Republic of the Philippines are the provinces, cities, municipalities, and Oaranqays. There shall be autonomous regions in Muslim Mindanao and the Cordilleras as hereinafter provided. Accordingly, Section 4 Of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, as amended (LGC), establishes that the provisions of the Code shall apply to all provinces, cities, municipalities, barangays, and other political subdivisions as may be created by law, and, to the extent herein provided, to officials, offices, or agencies of the national government. In connection therewith, the LGC classifies the barangay as a basic political unit6 and a body politic endowed with powers to be exercised by it in conformity with the law7. Furthermore, to implement the Constitutional mandate that territorial and political subdivisions shall enjoy local autonomy8, the LGUs have been granted several proprietary functions under Section 22 of the LGC. Among the numerous corporate powers that are granted to a barangay is the power to acquire and convey real and personal property, to wit: SECTION 22. corporate Powers. - (a) Every local government unit, as corporation. shall have the following powers: (I) xxx; (2) xxx; (3) xxx; (4) n xx xxx xxx (d) Local government units shall enjoy full autonomy in the Qsercise of their proprietprv functiqns and in the manaqement Of their economic enterprises. subject to 6 SECTION 384. Role Of the Barangay. — As the basic political unit, the barangay serves as the primary planning and implementing unit of government policies, plans, programs, projects, and activities in the community, and as a forum wherein the collective views of the people may be expressed, crystallized and considered, and where disputes may be amicably settled. 7 SECTION 15. Political and Corporate Nature Of Local Government Units. — Every local government unit created or recognized under this Code is a body politic and corporate endowed with powers to be exercised by it in conformity with law. As such, it shall exercise powers as a political subdivision of the national government and as a corporate entity representing the inhabitants of its territory. 8 SECTION 2. The territorial and political subdivisions shall enjoy local autonomy.

the limitations provided in this Code and other applicable laws. [Emphasis and underscoring supplied]. In view of the foregoing, it is evident that a barangay possesses corporate powers as a body politic by and through its officials in conformity with law. As such, aside from the fact that barangays have been given the power to exercise its governmental functions as a political subdivision of the national government, it has also been given the power to exercise proprietary functions or to act as a corporate entity representing the inhabitants of its territory. Therefore, as to your first query, it is undoubtedly clear that barangays have separate corporate personality from the respective cities and/or municipalities where it is located. As to the second issue on whether granting special patent under the name of barangay is not allowed and legally questionable. This Department would like to invite your attention to Section 7 of Republic Act No. 10023, otherwise known as The Free Patent Act, wherein it explicitly provides that the Director of the Land Management Bureau of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) to promulgate rules and regulations to carry out the provisions of such law. Hence, considering the afore-mentioned provision in the enabling law, this Department is of the considered view that DENR Administrative Order No. 2016-21 (DAO 2016-21) is a valid exercise of delegated legislative authority by the Secretary of the DENR. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, UTHORITY OF THE SECRET RY ARTIN B. DIN ersecretary for Barangay Affairs LLLS/32 COPY FURNISHED: LEOCADIO T.
